citation: Malek N, Mrowczynska E, Michrowska A, Mazurkiewicz E, Pavlyk I, Mazur AJ. Knockout of ACTB and ACTG1 with CRISPR/Cas9(D10A) Technique Shows that Non-Muscle beta and gamma Actin Are Not Equal in Relation to Human Melanoma Cells' Motility and Focal Adhesion Formation. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2020;21(8):2746. doi:10.3390/ijms21082746.
description: CRISPR inactivation of ACTB or ACTG1 in human melanoma cells showed that absence of one non-muscle actin isoform was compensated by increased expression of the other. This directly supports an expectation that Actb loss can raise Actg1 expression, although in a non-neuronal clonal cell system.

citation: Annayev Y, Adar S, Chiou YY, Lieb JD, Sancar A, Ye R. Gene model 129 encodes a novel transcriptional repressor that modulates circadian gene expression. Journal of Biological Chemistry. 2014;289(8):5013-5024. doi:10.1074/jbc.M113.534651.
description: This study describes the CLOCK-BMAL1 circadian transcriptional feedback loop and reports CLOCK-BMAL1 occupancy at a direct target whose perturbation shifts Nr1d1 and Dbp expression rhythms in mouse liver. It supports Bmal1-to-circadian-output interpretation for Dbp/Nr1d-family responses, with cell-type and sampling-time uncertainty.

citation: Radhakrishnan SK, Lee CS, Young P, Beskow A, Chan JY, Deshaies RJ. Transcription factor Nrf1 mediates the proteasome recovery pathway after proteasome inhibition in mammalian cells. Molecular Cell. 2010;38(1):17-28. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2010.02.029.
description: NFE2L1/NRF1 was required for induction of proteasome subunit genes and recovery of proteasome activity after proteasome inhibition in mammalian cells. This supplies a proteasome-stress feedback bridge for Psmc1/Psmc5/Nrf1 perturbations, but it does not define the full neuron-specific mixed modules observed here.

citation: Seddighi S, Qi YA, Brown AL, et al. Mis-spliced transcripts generate de novo proteins in TDP-43-related ALS/FTD. Science Translational Medicine. 2024;16(731):eadg7162. doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.adg7162.
description: Coordinated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses showed that TDP-43 depletion in human iPSC-derived neurons induces widespread cryptic exon-containing transcripts that can alter protein products. It supports a target-specific splicing-loss bridge for Tardbp perturbation but not a decisive prediction for the individual abundance changes measured by this 3-prime snRNA-seq screen.

citation: Lagier-Tourenne C, Polymenidou M, Hutt KR, et al. Divergent roles of ALS-linked proteins FUS/TLS and TDP-43 intersect in processing long pre-mRNAs. Nature Neuroscience. 2012;15(11):1488-1497. doi:10.1038/nn.3230.
description: This paper mapped FUS/TLS binding in mouse and human brain and showed that FUS depletion in the adult nervous system altered mRNA abundance or splicing for hundreds of genes. It provides a specific RNA-processing bridge for Fus loss, while leaving the direction of the observed Rsrp1/Atxn2l modules unresolved.

citation: Gehman LT, Stoilov P, Maguire J, et al. The splicing regulator Rbfox1 controls neuronal excitation in the mammalian brain. Nature Genetics. 2011;43(7):706-711. doi:10.1038/ng.841.
description: Central nervous system-specific Rbfox1 deletion in mouse altered whole-transcriptome splicing of synaptic and excitability genes and produced neuronal hyperexcitability. The study supports a neuron-specific post-transcriptional bridge for Rbfox1 perturbation, but it does not predict the 3-prime abundance changes in Adgrb1 or Hnrnpm seen here.

citation: Doggett K, Morgan KJ, Olthof AM, et al. Inhibition of the minor spliceosome restricts the growth of a broad spectrum of cancers. EMBO Reports. 2025;26:e70065. doi:10.1038/s44319-025-00511-8.
description: Rnpc3 heterozygosity or RNPC3 knockdown disrupted minor intron splicing and produced broad gene-expression consequences including replication stress, TP53 accumulation, cell-cycle arrest, and apoptosis. It gives a target-specific minor-spliceosome bridge for RNPC3 loss without specifying the neuronal Amy1/Mapk8/Pcyt2 abundance program.

citation: Becker D, Hirsch AG, Bender L, Lingner T, Salinas G, Krebber H. Nuclear Pre-snRNA Export Is an Essential Quality Assurance Mechanism for Functional Spliceosomes. Cell Reports. 2019;27(11):3199-3214.e3. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2019.05.031.
description: The authors showed that Xpo1-dependent pre-snRNA export is needed for spliceosomal snRNA maturation and that preventing export causes faulty spliceosome assembly and genome-wide splicing defects in yeast. This is a specific but indirect bridge from Xpo1 perturbation to RNA-processing stress in mammalian neurons.

citation: Shah S, Medisetti S, Fernandes JAL, Mattar P. Chd4 remodels chromatin to control retinal cell type specification and lineage termination. Development. 2025;152(21):dev204697. doi:10.1242/dev.204697.
description: Retina-specific Chd4 conditional knockout changed chromatin accessibility at thousands of regulatory elements and increased corresponding transcription during retinal development. The study links Chd4/NuRD to large transcriptional effects, but in proliferating retinal progenitors rather than acute postmitotic brain nuclei.

citation: Barbagiovanni G, Germain PL, Zech M, et al. KMT2B Is Selectively Required for Neuronal Transdifferentiation, and Its Loss Exposes Dystonia Candidate Genes. Cell Reports. 2018;25(4):988-1001.e9. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2018.09.067.
description: KMT2B inactivation during induced neuronal conversion altered the activation of neuronal maturation genes and exposed KMT2B-vulnerable targets. This gives a target-specific H3K4 methyltransferase-to-neuronal transcription bridge, but only in a developmental reprogramming system.
